clues: He was a prophet.
He called his people for a very long time.
Few of them believed him.
He was commanded to build something large.
He built an ark before the flood.
easy.explain: Nuh (Noah), ʿalayhi al-salām, called his people for many years before being commanded to build the ark. Surah Nuh is named after him.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was raised in a royal household that was not his own.
He was sent to a tyrant king.
He was given a scripture, the Tawrat.
His staff became a serpent, and the sea parted for him.
easy.explain: Musa (Moses), ʿalayhi al-salām, is the prophet most often named in the Qur'an. He was sent to Pharaoh and given the Tawrat.

clues: He was a prophet.
He had a dream as a child involving stars.
His brothers threw him into a well.
He later interpreted the dreams of a king.
A surah of the Qur'an is named after him and tells his story.
easy.explain: Surah Yusuf tells the story of Yusuf (Joseph), ʿalayhi al-salām, in one continuous narrative — unusual in the Qur'an.

clues: He was a prophet.
He is called a friend of Allah, Khalilullah.
He argued against the idols of his people.
He was thrown into a fire that was made cool for him.
He and his son raised the foundations of the Ka'bah.
easy.explain: Ibrahim (Abraham), ʿalayhi al-salām, is one of the five Ulul-Azm prophets. With his son Isma'il he raised the foundations of the Ka'bah.

clues: She is a woman mentioned in the Qur'an.
She is the only woman named in the Qur'an by her own name.
A surah is named after her.
She is described as chosen above the women of the worlds.
She is the mother of Prophet Isa.
easy.explain: Maryam is the only woman named by name in the Qur'an, and Surah Maryam (19) is named after her. She is the mother of Prophet Isa, ʿalayhi al-salām.

clues: It is a place in the hereafter.
It is the reward promised to the believers.
It is described as containing rivers.
It is entered after the Day of Judgement.
It is the garden, or paradise.
easy.explain: Jannah is paradise, the reward of the believers, described throughout the Qur'an as gardens beneath which rivers flow.

clues: It is the most central concept in Islam.
It concerns Allah alone.
It is the opposite of shirk.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is entirely about it.
It means the absolute oneness of Allah.
easy.explain: Tawhid is the affirmation of the absolute oneness of Allah, the foundation of Islamic belief and the opposite of shirk, associating partners with Him.

clues: It is a source of guidance in Islam.
It is not the Qur'an itself.
It concerns one particular person.
It refers to his sayings, actions and approvals.
It is the way of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
easy.explain: The Sunnah is the practice of the Prophet ﷺ — his sayings, actions and tacit approvals. Hadith are the reports through which the Sunnah is transmitted.

clues: It is a unit of something.
It belongs to the prayer.
Each one contains standing, bowing and prostrating.
Fajr has two of them.
Dhuhr has four of them.
easy.explain: A rak'ah is one complete unit of prayer. Fajr has two, Maghrib three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

clues: It is connected with fasting.
It happens at a precise moment each day.
It is traditionally begun with dates and water.
It takes place when the sun sets.
It is the meal that breaks the fast.
easy.explain: Iftar is the breaking of the fast at sunset, traditionally with dates and water, followed by the Maghrib prayer.

clues: It is a mosque.
It is in Madinah.
It was established by the Prophet ﷺ after the Hijrah.
It is the second holiest mosque in Islam.
The Prophet ﷺ is buried within it.
easy.explain: Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, was established after the Hijrah and is the second holiest mosque in Islam.

clues: It is a form of giving.
It is encouraged but not compulsory.
It has no fixed rate.
It can be given at any time, in any amount.
Even a smile is described as a form of it.
easy.explain: Sadaqah is voluntary charity, with no fixed amount or time. Zakat, by contrast, is the obligatory annual charity with defined rules.

clues: It is a division of the Qur'an.
It is larger than a single verse.
Each one has a name.
There are 114 of them.
The first is Al-Fatihah and the last is An-Nas.
easy.explain: A surah is a chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114, ranging from three ayahs (Al-Kawthar) to 286 (Al-Baqarah).

clues: It is a division of the Qur'an.
It is smaller than a chapter.
The word also means a sign.
They are numbered within each chapter.
There are over six thousand of them in total.
easy.explain: An ayah is a verse of the Qur'an; the word also means 'sign'. The commonly cited total is 6,236 in the Hafs reading.

clues: It is an event yet to come.
Belief in it is one of the articles of faith.
It follows the end of this world.
People will be raised and gathered.
Deeds will be weighed and recompensed.
easy.explain: Yawm al-Qiyamah, the Day of Judgement, is one of the six articles of faith. The dead are resurrected, gathered, and recompensed for their deeds.

clues: It is an act of worship.
It can be done at any time, anywhere.
It needs no fixed posture.
It involves repeating certain phrases.
It is the remembrance of Allah.
easy.explain: Dhikr is the remembrance of Allah through phrases such as SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar. It requires no fixed time or posture.

clues: It is an act of worship.
It can be made in any language.
It is personal rather than fixed in form.
It is described as the essence of worship.
It is calling upon Allah and asking of Him.
easy.explain: Du'a is supplication — calling upon Allah. It may be made in any language, at any time, and is described in hadith as the essence of worship.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was born without a father.
His mother is named in the Qur'an.
He was given a scripture, the Injil.
The Qur'an says he was raised up and not killed.
easy.explain: Isa (Jesus), ʿalayhi al-salām, is one of the Ulul-Azm prophets, born to Maryam without a father and given the Injil. The Qur'an states he was raised up rather than crucified.

clues: She is a woman in the Islamic tradition.
She was left in a barren valley with her infant son.
She searched desperately for water.
She ran between two hills seven times.
The well of Zamzam sprang for her son Isma'il.
easy.explain: Hajar's search for water between Safa and Marwah is commemorated in the rite of Sa'i, and the well of Zamzam is traditionally connected to it.

clues: It is a physical object.
It is treated with great respect.
It is the Qur'an in a particular form.
It is the Qur'an as a bound written copy.
The word distinguishes the book from the recitation itself.
easy.explain: The mus'haf is the Qur'an in written, bound form. The word distinguishes the physical copy from the Qur'an as recited revelation.

clues: It is a Makkan surah.
It has 110 ayahs.
It contains four distinct stories.
One concerns young men who slept in a cave for many years.
Many Muslims recite it on Fridays.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Kahf (18) contains the stories of the people of the cave, the man with two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn. Reciting it on Friday is a widespread practice.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of thirty ayahs.
It opens juz 29.
Its name refers to dominion or sovereignty.
It is commonly recited before sleeping.
It is described as interceding for the one who recites it.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mulk (67) has thirty ayahs and opens juz 29. It is widely recited before sleep, on the strength of narrations describing it as a protector for its reciter.

clues: He appears in Surah Al-Kahf.
He is not named outright in the Qur'an itself.
A prophet travelled with him to learn.
That prophet was Musa.
He performed three acts whose reasons were explained only at the end.
medium.explain: The figure travelling with Musa in Surah Al-Kahf is identified as al-Khidr in hadith rather than in the Qur'an, which calls him a servant granted knowledge from Allah. Scholars differ over whether he was a prophet.

clues: He appears in Surah Al-Kahf.
He was a powerful and just traveller-ruler.
He journeyed to the west, then to the east.
He encountered a people who asked him for help.
He built a barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj.
medium.explain: Dhul-Qarnayn is described in Surah Al-Kahf as a just ruler who built a barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj. His historical identity is debated and the Qur'an does not specify it.

clues: A surah of the Qur'an is named after him.
He is not generally counted among the prophets.
He was granted wisdom by Allah.
The surah records his advice to his son.
He warned his son against shirk above all.
medium.explain: Surah Luqman (31) records the counsel of Luqman the Wise to his son, beginning with a warning against shirk. He is generally regarded as a wise man rather than a prophet.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of 83 ayahs.
It is surah 36 in the mushaf.
It is widely memorised and frequently recited.
It is sometimes called the heart of the Qur'an.
Its name consists of two disconnected letters.
medium.explain: Surah Yasin (36) has 83 ayahs. It opens with the disconnected letters Ya-Sin, and is widely recited. Scholars differ on the authenticity of some narrations about its particular merits.

clues: They occur at the start of certain surahs.
There are twenty-nine surahs that begin with them.
They are recited letter by letter, not as words.
Alif-Lam-Mim is the best known example.
Their meaning is known to Allah alone, according to most scholars.
medium.explain: Al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at, the disconnected letters, open twenty-nine surahs. Most scholars hold their meaning to be known to Allah alone, though various interpretations have been offered.

clues: It is a term from the rules of zakat.
It is a quantity, not an action.
Below it, no zakat is due.
It is traditionally measured against gold or silver.
It is the minimum threshold of wealth.
medium.explain: The nisab is the minimum amount of wealth a person must hold before zakat becomes due, traditionally measured against set weights of gold or silver. The hawl is the lunar year that must pass over it.

clues: They are a group of leaders.
They led after the Prophet ﷺ.
There were four of them, by the usual count.
Their period lasted about thirty years.
Their name means the rightly-guided.
medium.explain: The Rashidun, the rightly-guided caliphs, are Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, whose combined rule spanned roughly 11 to 40 AH.

clues: It is a Madinan surah.
It is the longest surah in the Qur'an.
It has 286 ayahs.
It contains the longest verse in the Qur'an.
It contains Ayat al-Kursi.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah (2) is the longest surah at 286 ayahs. It contains Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) and the Qur'an's longest verse, the verse of debt (2:282).

clues: It is a category of narration.
It is transmitted through the Prophet ﷺ.
Its meaning is attributed to Allah.
Its wording is the Prophet's own.
It is nonetheless not part of the Qur'an.
medium.explain: A hadith qudsi conveys meaning attributed to Allah in the Prophet's own wording. It is distinct from the Qur'an, which is revealed in both meaning and exact wording.

clues: It is a technical term in hadith study.
Every narration has one.
It is not the content of the report.
It is examined to judge reliability.
It is the chain of narrators.
medium.explain: The isnad is the chain of narrators through which a hadith is transmitted; the matn is its text. Scholars assess both in grading a narration.

clues: It is a discipline of Islamic scholarship.
It concerns the Qur'an.
It is not about pronunciation.
It draws on language, context and narrations.
It is the explanation of the Qur'an's meaning.
medium.explain: Tafsir is the exegesis of the Qur'an, drawing on language, occasions of revelation, and narrations. Well-known works include those of al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir.

clues: It is a discipline concerning the Qur'an.
It is not about meaning.
It governs how the text is uttered.
It covers elongation, merging and nasalisation.
It is the science of correct recitation.
medium.explain: Tajwid governs the correct pronunciation of the Qur'an — the articulation points of letters and rules such as madd, idgham and ghunnah.

clues: It occurs within the prayer.
It is a supplication, not a movement.
It is most often associated with the Witr prayer.
It is also made at times of calamity.
It is typically made while standing, after rising from ruku.
medium.explain: Qunut is a supplication made while standing in prayer, most commonly in Witr. Schools differ on where and when it is recited.

clues: It is a financial duty in Islamic law.
It is owed to specific people, not the general poor.
It is not an annual calculation.
It concerns those in one's care.
It is the maintenance owed to one's dependants.
medium.explain: Nafaqah is the maintenance a person owes to their dependants — spouse, children and in some cases parents. It is distinct from zakat, which is owed to the eight Qur'anic categories.

clues: It relates to fasting.
It applies to those who cannot fast at all.
It applies, for example, to the chronically ill or the very elderly.
It is not a penalty for deliberate breaking of the fast.
It is feeding a needy person for each missed day.
medium.explain: Fidyah is the compensation of feeding a needy person for each fast a person is permanently unable to keep. Kaffarah is the heavier expiation for deliberately breaking a fast.

clues: It concerns an act of worship not performed on time.
It applies to prayers and to fasts.
It does not involve money.
A traveller or a sick person may need to do it.
It is making up what was missed, later.
medium.explain: Qada is making up a missed obligatory prayer or fast at a later time — for example, fasts missed during Ramadan due to illness or travel.

clues: It belongs to the rules of marriage.
It is given by the husband.
It is given to the wife herself, not her family.
It is her property to keep.
It is a required part of the marriage contract.
medium.explain: The mahr is the dower given by the husband to the wife as her own property. It is a requirement of the marriage contract and belongs to her alone.

clues: It is surah 55.
It falls in juz 27.
It opens with one of the names of Allah.
It enumerates blessings one after another.
A single verse is repeated thirty-one times within it.
medium.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman (55) repeats the refrain 'Then which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?' thirty-one times, between enumerated blessings.

clues: It took place in 7 AH.
It followed closely on a treaty.
It concerned a set of fortified settlements north of Madinah.
Ali ibn Abi Talib was given the banner.
The settlements were taken after a siege.
hard.explain: Khaybar, 7 AH, followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The fortified oasis settlements north of Madinah were taken after a siege, with Ali ibn Abi Talib given the banner.

clues: It was a pledge given before the Hijrah.
It was given by a small group from Yathrib.
It is sometimes called the pledge of the women.
Its terms concerned conduct, not warfare.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent back with them to teach.
hard.explain: The first Pledge of Aqabah committed a small group from Yathrib to belief and to abstaining from specified wrongs, without any undertaking to fight. Mus'ab ibn Umayr returned with them as a teacher.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of 129 ayahs.
It is the ninth surah.
It is the only surah not opened by the Basmalah.
It deals with treaties and with those who stayed behind.
Its themes connect closely with the expedition to Tabuk.
hard.explain: Surah At-Tawbah (9) is the only surah that does not begin with the Basmalah. Much of it addresses the aftermath of Tabuk and the conduct of those who did not join it.

clues: It concerns the written text of the Qur'an.
It took place very shortly after the Prophet's passing.
It was prompted by the deaths of many memorisers in battle.
Umar proposed it and Zayd ibn Thabit carried it out.
It gathered the Qur'an into a single written collection.
hard.explain: After many huffaz were killed at the Battle of Yamamah, Umar urged Abu Bakr to have the Qur'an gathered into one written collection, a task entrusted to Zayd ibn Thabit. Uthman's later work standardised and distributed copies.

clues: It concerns the written text of the Qur'an.
It happened about twenty years after the Prophet's passing.
It was prompted by differences arising in distant regions.
Official copies were produced and sent to the major centres.
Zayd ibn Thabit was again central to the work.
hard.explain: Uthman had standard copies prepared and sent to the main centres of the expanding state, in response to differences in recitation emerging among new Muslims in distant regions.

clues: It was fought after the Prophet's passing.
It took place during the caliphate of Abu Bakr.
It was part of the Ridda campaigns.
Many memorisers of the Qur'an were killed in it.
It prompted the gathering of the Qur'an into one collection.
hard.explain: Yamamah, fought during Abu Bakr's caliphate against the forces of Musaylimah, cost the lives of many huffaz — which directly prompted the written compilation of the Qur'an.

clues: It was fought during the Rashidun period.
It was fought against the Byzantines.
It took place near a river in the Levant.
Khalid ibn al-Walid played a decisive role.
It opened the way to Muslim control of Syria.
hard.explain: Yarmuk, fought around 15 AH against the Byzantines, was decisive in bringing Syria under Muslim control. Khalid ibn al-Walid's command is widely credited for the outcome.

clues: It was fought during Umar's caliphate.
It was fought against the Sasanian empire, not the Byzantines.
It took place in Iraq.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas commanded the Muslim force.
It opened the way into Persia.
hard.explain: Qadisiyyah, fought in Iraq under the command of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas during Umar's caliphate, was decisive against the Sasanian empire.

clues: They were a group in Madinah.
They were companions of the Prophet ﷺ.
They had no homes of their own.
They lived on a shaded platform attached to the mosque.
They devoted themselves to learning and worship.
hard.explain: The Ashab al-Suffah were poor companions who lived on a raised, shaded platform at the Prophet's Mosque, devoting themselves to learning. Abu Hurayrah was among them.

clues: The term refers to a group connected to the Prophet ﷺ.
It is not defined by city of origin.
It is mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab.
Its exact scope is discussed by scholars.
It means the people of the household.
hard.explain: Ahl al-Bayt refers to the household of the Prophet ﷺ, mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab 33:33. Scholars differ on precisely whom the term encompasses.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of eighteen ayahs.
Its subject is conduct between people.
It addresses how to behave towards the Prophet ﷺ.
It forbids mockery, suspicion and backbiting.
It states that the most honoured are the most God-fearing.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hujurat (49) sets out norms of conduct: verifying news, reconciling disputes, avoiding mockery, suspicion and backbiting, and the principle that honour lies in taqwa, not lineage.

clues: It is a field within Qur'anic studies.
It concerns context rather than wording.
It records the circumstances in which verses came down.
It helps clarify the intent of particular passages.
It is known in Arabic as asbab al-nuzul.
hard.explain: Asbab al-nuzul records the circumstances in which particular verses were revealed. It assists interpretation, though scholars caution that a verse's ruling is not limited to its occasion.

clues: It was an agreement made in Makkah.
It was made before the Prophet's mission began.
He took part in it as a young man.
It was a pact among clans to aid the wronged.
He later said he would still answer such a call in Islam.
hard.explain: Hilf al-Fudul was a pre-Islamic pact among Makkan clans to support anyone wronged in the city. The Prophet ﷺ participated in his youth and later spoke approvingly of it.

clues: It took place in Makkah before the Hijrah.
It was directed at two clans of the Quraysh.
It lasted roughly three years.
It cut off trade and marriage with them.
Its terms were written and posted in the Ka'bah.
hard.explain: The Quraysh imposed a boycott on Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib for roughly three years, its terms written on a document hung in the Ka'bah. The hardship it caused preceded the Year of Sorrow.

clues: It was a journey undertaken from Makkah.
It took place in the late Makkan period.
Its purpose was to seek support from another town.
The Prophet ﷺ was rejected and driven out.
He returned saying he complained of his weakness only to Allah.
hard.explain: After the Year of Sorrow, the Prophet ﷺ travelled to Ta'if seeking support and was rejected and pelted. The episode is remembered particularly for his supplication on the return journey.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-four ayahs.
Its name refers to a gathering or exile.
It praises the Ansar for preferring others over themselves.
It warns against being like those who forgot Allah.
Its final three verses enumerate names of Allah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hashr (59) closes with three verses enumerating many of the names and attributes of Allah, and earlier praises the Ansar for preferring others over themselves despite their own need.

clues: It is a concept in Qur'anic and legal study.
It concerns rulings over time.
It applies within the period of revelation.
Scholars differ considerably over its extent.
It is the abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later one.
hard.explain: Naskh is the abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later revelation. Its existence is broadly accepted, but scholars differ substantially over how many verses it affects.

clues: It is one of the sources of Islamic law.
It ranks after the Qur'an and the Sunnah.
It is not individual reasoning.
It concerns the position of the scholars collectively.
It is consensus.
hard.explain: Ijma is the consensus of qualified scholars, conventionally the third source of law after the Qur'an and Sunnah. Qiyas, analogical reasoning, is usually listed fourth.

clues: It is one of the sources of Islamic law.
It is conventionally listed fourth.
It is used when no direct text addresses a matter.
It extends an existing ruling to a new case.
It works by identifying a shared underlying cause.
hard.explain: Qiyas is analogical reasoning: extending a ruling from a case addressed by the texts to a new case sharing the same effective cause ('illah). The Zahiri school rejected it.

clues: It is a very short Makkan surah.
It has three ayahs.
It opens with an oath.
It states that mankind is in loss, with exceptions.
Al-Shafi'i said that if people reflected on it alone it would suffice them.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Asr (103) has three ayahs: an oath by time, the declaration that mankind is in loss, and the four exceptions — faith, righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and to patience.
